create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified in the authorization or token request, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag missing JWT claims or inability to locally validate as a bug in this case; use introspection or request a resource to obtain a JWT.

oidc_jwt.description: Tokens issued later through refresh can only contain a subset of scopes requested in the original OAuth flow.
oidc_jwt.source: Authorization fragment on scope subset rule.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing newly granted scopes after refresh is by design if they were not in the original request.

oidc_jwt.description: If organization_id is omitted from the token request, only global roles and permissions are evaluated.
oidc_jwt.note: Access without organization RBAC in such a request is by design, not an org-boundary bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured, omitting the resource parameter causes Logto to use that default audience.
oidc_jwt.note: A token accepted for the default audience after omitting resource is expected behavior, not audience confusion.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not modify already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated permissions.
oidc_jwt.note: A valid old token continuing to work until expiration is by design and should not be reported as stale authorization unless a newly issued token also ignores the change.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, refresh does not add newly granted scopes unless they were already part of the original authorization request set.
oidc_jwt.note: Use a new authorization flow when testing newly granted global scopes outside the original request.

oidc_jwt.description: When permissions are reduced, existing JWTs keep their old scopes until they expire; only newly issued tokens reflect downscoped permissions.
oidc_jwt.source: Authorization fragment on handling user permission change.
oidc_jwt.note: A valid tightening test must compare newly issued tokens after the change, not expect already-issued JWTs to mutate.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session clears the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access may remain valid until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: A refresh token continuing to work after browser sign-out can be by design when offline_access was granted.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct_sign_in references a missing or disabled connector, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat fallback to hosted sign-in as a flow confusion bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing users signing in with enterprise SSO are automatically linked to the existing Logto account when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Cross-source identity merge on matching email is documented behavior, not necessarily an identity-collision vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Social connector target values determine whether identities from connectors are treated as the same source or separate sources.
oidc_jwt.note: Same target can merge identities across connectors; different targets can intentionally split the same upstream IdP into separate Logto accounts.

oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same JWT bearer token is generally possible until expiry because Logto-issued JWT access tokens are stateless bearer tokens unless a special one-time exchange flow is used.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token and authorization docs describe JWT access tokens as bearer tokens; replay tracking is not documented for ordinary JWT access tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token on ordinary JWT bearer access tokens as a vulnerability by itself.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer replay detection via jti tracking is not documented as enforced for standard JWT access tokens; stateless validation is expected.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay of the same JWT as a vulnerability absent a documented one-time-use guarantee.

oidc_jwt.description: If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.source: Opaque token concept and RBAC docs on default API behavior.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not treat non-JWT access tokens in no-resource flows as a token-format bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission changes do not retroactively modify already-issued JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect updated permissions.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag stale old-token permissions as a coherence bug unless the same request is inconsistently evaluated under the same token.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Logto's OIDC provider is mounted at /oidc, and direct OIDC API calls should use Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded for token, introspection, and revocation requests. Sending JSON may fail or be misinterpreted.
oidc_jwt.source: Core Service / OIDC Provider docs and token examples

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL token request that should succeed under the same client/application setup. A failed attack token alone is ambiguous because Logto also rejects requests for unrelated reasons such as missing resource, missing organization context, or disabled grant configuration.

The resource parameter must EXACTLY match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). No wildcard, prefix, or shortened matching is documented. For I5 audience tests, use exact registered URIs only; do not assume partial matches.

Scope names must EXACTLY match permission names defined on the API resource. Logto does not support wildcard or prefix matching for scopes. For I5 authorization-binding tests, request the full exact scope names and do not use abbreviated values like read or write unless those are the actual permission names.

Organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated. For I5 organization-bound tests, the fuzzer MUST include organization_id on the token request; otherwise a pass/fail result does not test organization authorization at all.

Organization permissions and organization-level API permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. For I5 tests, do not interpret absence of organization permissions in a global token as a bug; use separate test setups for global and organization-scoped authorization.
oidc_jwt.source: Organization permissions and organization-level API resources docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: When no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT. Opaque tokens are intended for /oidc/me and require /oidc/token/introspection for validation. For oidc_jwt tests that require JWT claim manipulation or JWT audience checks, the fuzzer MUST request a specific resource or organization token so that Logto returns a JWT.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. To obtain an organization token for a user, first get a refresh token from authorization_code, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Tests that expect organization claims immediately after code exchange will be misconfigured.
oidc_jwt.source: Organization token warning and organization permissions docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For global API resources, enlarged permissions do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the originally requested scope set; a new OAuth authorization flow is required for newly granted scopes outside the original request. For I3 config-change tests, do not expect refresh_token alone to pick up newly added scopes if the original authorization request did not include them.

For organization tokens, enlarged permissions appear on next issuance (refresh or token request), but still only within the originally requested scope set. For I3/I5 tests, distinguish between permission changes that should appear on refresh and changes that require a new authorization request because the new scopes were never requested originally.

Existing JWTs keep old scopes until they expire; permission reductions only affect newly issued tokens immediately. For I3 config-tightening tests, the fuzzer MUST obtain a NEW token after the change and must not treat continued acceptance of an already-issued JWT as stale-policy vulnerability.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any RFC 8693 token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, or the endpoint will fail with a configuration error unrelated to the security property under test.

PAT token exchange and impersonation token exchange both use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, but subject_token_type differs. For I5 token-exchange tests, set subject_token_type exactly to the documented value for the token being exchanged; otherwise failures are setup errors, not audience or scope enforcement results.
oidc_jwt.source: Personal access token and user impersonation docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: The token exchange request may authenticate the client either with HTTP Basic auth or with client_id in the form body for public clients. Use one valid client-auth method consistently. Missing or invalid client authentication causes token exchange failure unrelated to the exchanged token's audience or scope.
oidc_jwt.source: Personal access token and user impersonation examples

oidc_jwt.constraint: For impersonation-style token exchange, the subject token is documented as short-lived and one-time-use. Reusing the same subject token across multiple attack attempts can fail by design. For I2/I5 tests, mint a fresh subject token for each exchange attempt.

Logto validates issuer during JWT verification, but many example libraries disable automatic audience verification and require manual audience checks. For I5 audience-binding tests against applications using Logto-issued JWTs, the relying API must explicitly validate aud against the expected resource indicator or organization audience; otherwise an apparent acceptance may reflect incomplete verifier configuration, not a Logto issuance bug.
oidc_jwt.source: Validate access tokens in API docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC issuer and JWKS URI are fixed by the tenant endpoint and not customizable. For I1 trust-anchor and issuer-substitution tests, use the tenant's discovery document values as the only legitimate issuer/JWKS pair; any alternate issuer should be rejected.
oidc_jwt.source: Retrieve info about your Logto tenant

oidc_jwt.constraint: The .NET validation example sets ClockSkew to 5 minutes. If a relying API follows that example, tokens slightly past exp may still validate. For I2 expired_token tests against such integrations, use expiration offsets well beyond 300 seconds to avoid false positives caused by verifier leeway rather than Logto behavior.
Logto's OIDC provider is mounted under /oidc, and the UserInfo endpoint is /oidc/me rather than the more common /userinfo. The fuzzer MUST use the documented Logto paths exactly.
For OIDC token requests to /oidc/token and token revocation/introspection requests, the request body MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded. Sending JSON will not match the documented API.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, include a CONTROL token request and validation path alongside the attack case. Without a valid control token, a rejection cannot be distinguished from bad client_id/resource/scope/organization_id setup.

The resource parameter uses exact resource-indicator matching only. The resource value in authorization or token requests MUST exactly match the registered API identifier URI; wildcard-like or shortened values do not broaden matching.

Scope names use exact string matching only. Requested scopes MUST exactly match permission names defined in Logto; prefixes or partial names are not wildcards. For I5 tests, do not assume read matches read:products.

When testing organization-level authorization, organization RBAC is applied only if organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated, which would create false positives for organization-binding tests.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. To test organization permissions after interactive login, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters.

If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. JWT-focused tests for oidc_jwt MUST request a specific resource or organization token path that yields JWTs; otherwise failures may be due to token format, not security validation.

For organization tokens, Logto always uses JWT format because organization-specific claims must be validated by resource servers. The fuzzer SHOULD use organization_id when it needs JWT organization context and MUST NOT treat opaque tokens as organization tokens.

For I5 permission-change and scope-escalation tests, Logto enforces a scope subset rule: a newly issued access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test enlarged permissions correctly, the initial authorization request MUST already include the superset of scopes under test.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running token_exchange tests, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise failures are expected configuration errors rather than security findings.

For token exchange using personal access tokens, subject_token_type MUST be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. Using a different subject_token_type changes the semantics and invalidates the test.

For I5 audience-binding tests, APIs must validate aud against the registered API resource indicator and, for organization APIs, also validate organization_id context. A token with only organization context or only API audience is insufficient for organization-level API authorization.

Logto validates issuer against the tenant OIDC issuer URL and JWKS from the tenant JWKS URI. For I1 trust-anchor-substitution tests, the fuzzer must keep issuer and JWKS anchored to the same tenant and treat forged issuer/JWKS pairs as attack inputs, not alternate valid configurations.

Logto documentation shows audience verification may be performed manually by the protected API depending on permission model. A failed audience-mismatch test against a sample app may reflect missing API-side audience checks rather than IdP token issuance behavior; interpret results at the correct layer.

The documented .NET sample sets ClockSkew to 5 minutes for JWT lifetime validation. Freshness tests near exp/nbf boundaries may be accepted by sample integrations due to verifier leeway; use timestamps well outside any possible skew window when testing expired_token or future_token.
Logto does not support using applications themselves as authorization resources. I5 tests must target API resources identified by resource indicators, not application IDs as audiences.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL token flow that is known-good. Logto validation requires correct signature, issuer, expiration, and audience/context checks; a failing attack token without a control cannot distinguish freshness rejection from bad resource/scope/setup.
The /oidc/token endpoint requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests. Do not send JSON bodies for authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials, or token_exchange grants.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter must exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). Do not use prefixes, shortened values, or wildcard-like variants; exact URI match is required.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested scope names must exactly match the permission names defined in the API resource. Wildcards, prefixes, or shortened names are not supported; omit unsupported scopes rather than approximating them.

For I5 empty_audience tests, Logto issues opaque access tokens when no resource is specified, except when a default API resource is configured. To test JWT audience enforcement, request a specific resource or ensure a default API resource is configured; otherwise you may get an opaque token instead of a JWT.

Sentinel behavior: if no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT; if a default API resource is configured, omission of resource causes that default audience to be used. Never assume missing resource means 'any audience JWT'.

For organization-scoped I5 tests, organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization code flow. You must first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters, or use client_credentials with organization_id.

For organization RBAC tests, including organization_id changes authorization semantics. Without organization_id, only global roles/permissions are evaluated; with organization_id, Logto evaluates organization roles and emits organization context in the token. Do not compare these as the same policy context.

For I3 permission-change sequences, JWT permission changes only appear in newly issued tokens. Existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry. A valid coherence test must obtain a NEW token after the config or role change; do not expect already-issued JWTs to mutate.

For I5 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, refresh cannot add scopes that were not requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test newly granted scopes, run a new authorization flow with the expanded scope set; refresh alone is insufficient.

For I5 organization-token tests, organization permissions cannot be mixed with global API permissions in the same authorization model. Use organization template permissions for organization tokens and global permissions for global API tokens; mixing them will misconfigure the test.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before running RFC 8693 tests, enable 'Allow token exchange' on the target application, otherwise failures are expected and not evidence of a security control.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare exchanged token scopes/claims against the original authorization intent. PAT-obtained and refresh-token-obtained access tokens are documented as equivalent in authorization behavior, so differences should be attributed to requested resource/scope/context rather than grant family.

For I4 cross-user collision tests involving usernames, tenant-level CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME controls whether usernames are case-sensitive. 'Admin' vs 'admin' may be BY CONFIG rather than a collision bug; record the tenant setting before interpreting results.

For I4 enterprise SSO identity tests, Logto automatically links an enterprise SSO identity to an existing user account when the working email matches. Different upstream identities sharing the same email may intentionally collapse into one Logto user; do not flag this as a collision unless email differs.

For I1 issuer-validation tests against Logto-issued tokens, issuer is fixed to https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc and is discoverable from /oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration. Validation logic must compare against this exact issuer value, not the bare tenant origin.

For I1 audience tests in sample validators, many examples disable library-level audience verification and require manual audience checks. A test harness must explicitly validate aud against the API resource indicator or organization audience/context; otherwise audience-mismatch tests are meaningless.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications. SAML apps: /api/saml-applications.
